questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1. You find the courses you want to register for
2. You fill out a form and send it to the exchange office at VU
3. The courses you want are added to your personal vu rooster
4. When the registration period begins, you just sign up for the courses in your personal rooster 

(I had a bit of back an forth cause the schedules for the courses I wanted did not match, but it was still an okay process. The preffered us to do minor programs, which I did not do, and they were a bit less helpfull with selecting individual courses and getting the schedules to fit)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exhchange office coordinators by email or on wednesday between 12 and 13 I think

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was overall succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't want to spend to much time on it just follow a minor, but if you're okay with spending a bit more energy and time you can get some really really interesting courses if you pick sepperate courses instead of following a premade minor. So decide for yourslef before choosing how important the specific courses are for you and if they are worth the extra energy. It was for me, but I think you have to keep that in mind, cause it took me a lot of time and energy.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the course material a little bit easier than at my home institution. However I found it difficult taking the exams, cause the examination form was very different from the one I'm used to. Furthermore I found it very difficult to understand how much I needed to know for the exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very similar

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Experimental Cell Biology I
Experimental CellBiology II
Brain in Trouble
The Developing Brain
Biomedical Sciences and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in neuro and more specifically neuroscience and psyciatric disorders, then the two courses "Brain in Trouble" and "The Developing Brain" are really good. I found the courses interesting and challenging in a good way. You learn about the human mind, different personalities/personality traits, psyciatric disorders and you learn about how it relates to the brain and your nervous system. I really enjoyed these two courses and would definetly recommend them to anyone interested in human behavior, psyciatric disorders, brain development and neuroscience. Very interesting lectures!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Museums (my favorite was the Van Gogh museum, but many many great museums in Amsterdam. The Anne Frank house is really nice and Museumsplein is a great place if you like museums)
Go to Jordaan a really nice area with canals, nice shops and cozy cafés
Go to the Albert Cuyp market. You can get some really good both dutch and non-dutch food and you should definetly get a freshly made stroop wafel
Take a walk in the Pijp. Many nice restaurants, bars and cafées
For partying Amsterdam has a great night-life as well. So if you enjoy partying take a night out and experience Amsterdam party life.
If the weather is nice, then rent or borrow a bike and take a bikeride around the city. You get to see a lot of Amsterdam and experience it like a local on the bike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join for everything possible in the beginning. That's how you met new people. However the dutch students are not that interested in socializing with internationals, so expect to make a lot of international friends and not that many dutch friends...

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's very similar to my home country, so that made it easy and nice to adapt.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to find student accomodation where you meet other people. Dorms with shared kitchen is a good opportunity to meet new people when you're alone in a foreign country. 
2. Buy a museumcard if you like going to museums.
3. Rent a bike. Biking is the easiest and cheapest way to get around the city. Most exchange students rent via Swapfiets, that works really well!

And just remember to enjoy it! You're in an amazing city and country. Try to get all the experiences you can and enjoy your time abroad :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It might feel a bit overwhelming at times especially in the beginning, but talk to the other exchange students (they definetly feel the same). And try to join as many activities as possible in the beggining, cause this is the time to socialize and meet people that you can hopefully enjoy the next 5-6 months with. 

There are many other cities around Amsterdam that are also really nice, so I also really recommend taking small day trips. Fx. Utrecht, Zaandam, Harleem, Den Haag, Leiden, Rotterdam and Delft.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the experiences and friendships I got from it

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The way exams are done at VU and trying to balance new friends, new country and new university all at once

questions.answer: Yes
